correctness.rationale: Direct decomposition of harmonic quadratics into four O(p)×O(q) sectors accounts for the full dimension; the radial random variable is exactly Beta(p/2,q/2). All five normalized pairwise density differences are integrated by an exact boundary-derivative identity, proving the three crossings and their order for all distinct integer p,q≥3. The endpoint Beta asymptotic proves the sharp constant. A symbolic generic-parameter check and 18 independently built finite Gram eigensystems agree, with maximum numerical discrepancy below 9e-16. The finite checks are corroboration rather than an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is an exact unbalanced, ambient-volume cap spectrum and all-dimensional equispaced transition law. The closest published Clifford hypersurface theorem gives equal-block boundary-only traces: its equal-block spectral profile is NOT treated as new, and p=q is excluded. The known one-coordinate double-cap theorem has a 1-dimensional block and only three sectors, while general Slepian frameworks provide construction or bounds and do not state the unbalanced three-crossing phase diagram. Distinctness is substantiated at the level of domains, measures, hypotheses and implication, with historical-priority risk explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Older generalized bi-spherical Jacobi spectral decompositions could implicitly yield the unbalanced Beta cap ordering, even when not found with targeted searches.
Complete Roddy–McEwen 2021 source was not inspected because the available PDF exceeded the retrieval limit; it is principally a wavelet construction paper, but the limitation is explicit.
No exhaustive global priority certification is possible from the indexed literature and published records alone.

value.rationale: A full infinite two-parameter classification for observation tubes about subspheres: four sectors, three exactly equispaced spectral crossing thresholds with equality multiplicities, two sharp extremal switches, and a closed-form inverse-instability constant. Useful for distinguishing recoverable quadrupolar symmetries under partial-sphere observations; unlike a single numeric invariant, it solves the sharp operator ordering for all unbalanced integer block dimensions at least three. Equal-block cases implied by old boundary spectra are deliberately excluded.
